metadata.note: Corbin's Manhattan Beach system in Brooklyn and Ridgewood: the New York and Manhattan Beach Railway's narrow-gauge era (1877-1882) and the Long Island Rail Road's Manhattan Beach Division (1883-1924). Drawn only to the research report's drawable spans (research/branches/manhattan_beach_railway.txt). Features split at the 1882/1883 operator change share identical geometry (Rule 4).
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (live Bay Ridge Branch / Fremont Industrial Track; abandoned ways 601377483, 295951391, 295951390; razed way 601392952), traced with opstrace.py
hand-placed straight legs where the line is lifted and unmapped (named per feature in geometry_quality)
metadata.ownership_split: 1882/1883: New York and Manhattan Beach Railway to 1882, Long Island Rail Road from 1883, following Chiasson (May 1883 the 'first operational season under LIRR auspices') over the Dec 1881 lease date (Wikipedia). The 1885 New York, Brooklyn & Manhattan Beach merger/lease and the 1925 merger into the LIRR are paper changes, not operator changes.
not_yet_sourced: Bay Ridge passenger end: 1897 (Chiasson, drawn) vs 14 May 1924 (Wikipedia station table; Emery's MB section). Needs an LIRR public timetable of c.1898-1923; the Brooklyn Daily Eagle was not searched.
1882 season operator: LIRR lease Dec 1881 (Wikipedia) vs first LIRR-run season 1883 (Chiasson). Drawn as NY&MB through 1882.
Greenpoint start 16 May 1878 (Chiasson, Wikipedia) vs 1879 (Emery); Greenpoint shuttle end Sep 1885 (Chiasson, drawn) vs 8 May 1886 (Emery).
Parkville Jct - Manhattan Beach Jct after 6 Oct 1902: the 1904 '4 trains a day from 65th St Ferry' are cited but doubted by Chiasson; not drawn.
1909 Manhattan Beach terminal opening: 19 Jun 1909 vs 29 Jul 1909 (both Chiasson). Geometry only.
Every headway_min is an estimate; only Chiasson's counts (13 trips each way 1877; 67/day division-wide 1897; 8/day 1910; 4/day 1913; 3/day 1918; 2 round trips 1921-24) are sourced.
Cooper Ave - East River mileage: '~3 mi' in the LIRR research file (Emery) vs c.4.2 mi drawn and c.3.8 mi straight-line; the published figure is not credible for Cooper Ave and is unresolved.
Long Island City - Fresh Pond Jct (LIRR Montauk Division), over which the 1883-1924 LIC trains ran, is drawn neither here nor in lirr.geojson.
Manhattan Beach Hotel and Oriental Hotel sites and the pre-1909 crossing of Sheepshead Bay are placed approximately; no surveyed alignment was found.
omitted: Block 4: New York, Bay Ridge & Jamaica 1876 season (Bay Ridge - Bath Jct, BB&WE trackage to Coney Island) - a different company's single season; omitted by instruction.
Block 9: BRT Sheepshead Bay - Manhattan Beach shuttle 1899-1903 (Brooklyn Rapid Transit trains over LIRR track) - another company; no BRT layer yet.
Block 10: BRT Brighton Line diversion over the branch 1906-1908 - another company's construction diversion.
Block 11: Culver Line under LIRR 1893-1899 - deferred to a Culver Line research pass.
Block 12: Marine Railway (Manhattan Beach - Brighton Beach) - a separate company; low priority, largely unplaceable.

Block 13: Kings County Central 'Prospect Park Division' 1878 [ANCHOR] - not drawn: its alignment is undocumented, and even its junction is uncertain (New York Ave per the report's block 13, a transfer 'next to the stop at Flatlands' i.e. Flatbush Ave per Chiasson May 2016), so it cannot be placed honestly.
Block 14: Sheepshead Bay Race Track spur 1909 [OPEN]-1910 - deferred; under 1 mi and unplaced.
metadata.freight_only: Not drawn (Rule 1): Bay Ridge - Parkville after 1897, Parkville - MB Jct after 1902, MB Jct - East New York - Fresh Pond after 13 May 1924 (New Haven/NY Connecting freight, today's NY&A), the Manhattan Beach Branch 1924-1935 freight, the Greenpoint end's freight after 1885 and the Evergreen Branch after 1894, and the 65th Street float yard.
metadata.horsecar: None on this road: all NYBR&J/NY&MB/LIRR service here was steam (Rule 5). The Bushwick horse operation in Emery is the South Side RR's, not this line.

properties.geometry_quality: Bay Ridge (65th St) - Parkville Jct - Manhattan Beach Jct (2.92 + 0.95 mi) traced from live OSM track (opstrace.py over OSM rail; every waypoint 0.0 km from the drawn line, no straight-line leg): the present freight-only Bay Ridge Branch (New York & Atlantic) and, north of Myrtle Ave, the Fremont Industrial Track to Fresh Pond Jct. Documented: Bay Ridge - Parkville ~3 mi and Parkville - MB Jct ~2 mi are the research report's own map estimates, not published figures; the trace's 0.95 mi for Parkville (McDonald Ave) - MB Jct (Ocean Ave) is the real distance between those streets. MB Jct (Ocean Ave/Ave I) follows OSM razed way 601392952 'Manhattan Beach Branch' for 0.13 mi; south of it the branch was lifted 1938-41 and neither OSM nor OpenHistoricalMap has it, so it is APPROXIMATED by hand-placed straight legs a few dozen metres east of the BMT Brighton Line (deliberately NOT snapped to the Brighton subway tracks, which are another company's): Ave I/E 16th St - South Greenfield (Ave M) 0.72 mi, South Greenfield - Kings Highway 0.64 mi, Kings Highway - Neck Road 0.93 mi, Neck Road - Sheepshead Bay 0.60 mi, Sheepshead Bay - Sheepshead Bay inlet (E 16th St/Emmons Ave) 0.24 mi, inlet - West End Ave & Oriental Blvd 0.44 mi, West End Ave & Oriental Blvd - Manhattan Beach Hotel (approx. site) 0.40 mi, Manhattan Beach Hotel - Oriental Hotel (approx. site) 0.46 mi. Total 8.42 mi, of which 4.42 mi approximated. Fit: South Greenfield - Manhattan Beach Hotel draws 3.25 mi against 3.23 mi documented (Wikipedia station table from the 16 Jun 1908 employee timetable: South Greenfield MP 12.87, Manhattan Beach MP 16.10). This feature draws the ORIGINAL 1877-1908 terminal approach east along the shore to the Oriental Hotel (alignment (a)), which is right for its era; the hotel sites are approximate. The 1907-09 relocation onto an embankment on the east side of the Brighton Line moved the branch north of Sheepshead Bay by about a block at most; at this approximation the pre- and post-1909 lines are not distinguishable. The line was regraded into an open cut / onto embankment in the 1905-1918 Bay Ridge Improvements; the drawn plan alignment is today's, substantially the original. The Bay Ridge end is drawn to the OSM end of track inside today's 65th Street Yard, c.0.3 mi short of the old ferry slip at the foot of 65th St.

segments.note: 3-ft gauge steam, summer seasons only. Opened 18 Jul 1877 with 13 trips a day each way from both Bay Ridge (boats from Manhattan) and East New York to the Oriental Hotel (Chiasson, ERA Bulletin Apr 2016); the 1882 season, the last narrow-gauge season, ended Oct 1882 (Chiasson May 2016). Built by the New York, Bay Ridge & Jamaica (Bay Ridge - Manhattan Beach Jct, leased to the NY&MB) and the NY&MB (the branch). The 1876 NYBR&J standard-gauge season Bay Ridge - Bath Jct is not drawn. The 1882/1883 operator split is UNRESOLVED: the LIRR leased the system in Dec 1881 (Wikipedia) but Chiasson calls May 1883 the first season 'under LIRR auspices'; this layer follows Chiasson. The headway is an ESTIMATE (Rule 3), not timetable-derived (about 13 trips each way in a c.14-hour day in 1877).
sources: Segment-level: dates and frequency from Chiasson, ERA NY Division Bulletin Apr 2016 and May 2016; opening date also Wikipedia.

segments.note: Standard-gauged and double-tracked for the 1883 season; first LIRR-run season. Trains from Long Island City via the Montauk Division and Fresh Pond Jct began 2 Jun 1883 (Wikipedia; Chiasson, ERA Bulletin May 2016); Flatbush Ave - Manhattan Beach trains via the Atlantic Division ran 30 May 1883 - Oct 1899 and join this line at East New York (their western leg is the LIRR Atlantic Branch, drawn elsewhere). Year-round service from Sept 1883. Peak about 1897: 67 trains a day across the whole division in summer (Chiasson Jul 2016). The headway is an ESTIMATE (Rule 3), not timetable-derived, derived from the 1897 division-wide summer count.
sources: Segment-level: dates from Chiasson, ERA NY Division Bulletin May 2016 and Jul 2016, and Wikipedia; frequency only as a division-wide count.

Original grade-level terminal approach to the Oriental Hotel used through 1908; LIRR track east of Oriental Blvd abandoned c.1908 (Emery). segments.note: Standard gauge from 1883: Bay Ridge (65th St ferry) - Manhattan Beach boat trains. Winter service tried Oct 1889 - Sept 1893, then dropped (Chiasson, ERA Bulletin May 2016). Culver (Prospect Park & Coney Island) trains also ran into Bay Ridge 1885-87 - another company's trains, not drawn. END 1897 per Chiasson (Jul 2016): 'no passenger service at all on the Bay Ridge Branch after that same season', beach trains moving to the 39th St Ferry from May 1898; Minn has the Bay Ridge ferry ending 1898. CONFLICT: Wikipedia's Bay Ridge Branch station table closes Bay Ridge and Third Ave on 14 May 1924, and Emery has a 'last passenger train from Bay Ridge to Manhattan Beach: 5/13/1924' (but a blank for Bay Ridge - Ocean Ave). The 1910 Official Guide and Chiasson's 1915 station list show no Bay Ridge service. Drawn to 1897, the shorter confirmed span; 1898-1924 is NOT claimed. Do not extend without a c.1898-1923 timetable showing Bay Ridge trains. Freight continues to the present (Rule 1: not drawn). The headway is an ESTIMATE (Rule 3), not timetable-derived.
sources: Segment-level: end year from Chiasson, ERA NY Division Bulletin Jul 2016 (with Minn's 1898 ferry end); conflicting 1924 dates from Wikipedia and Emery recorded in the note.
